items.title: Selected-size conditional validity yields a conditionally superuniform p-value
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P_0)$ be a probability space, let
$\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the interim sigma-algebra, let
$N$ be an $\mathcal F_1$-measurable sample size taking values in a nonempty
set $M\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$, and let $p_N$ be the selected stage-2 p-value. For
$m\in M$, put $D_m=\{N=m\}$. Suppose that for every $m\in M$, every fixed
$u\in[0,1]$, and every $H\in\mathcal F_1$,
$$P_0(H\cap D_m\cap\{p_N\le u\})\le uP_0(H\cap D_m).$$
Then for every fixed $u\in[0,1]$,
$$E_0[\mathbf1_{\{p_N\le u\}}\mid\mathcal F_1]\le u\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
Thus conditional validity within each selected-size stratum implies
conditional superuniformity after an interim-measurable finite sample size is
selected, even when the set of allowed sample sizes is countably infinite.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** partition the event by selected sample size, then use the defining event integrals to verify the conditional bound.

1.1 Fix $u\in[0,1]$ and $H\in\mathcal F_1$. The event $\{p_N\le u\}$ is measurable by the p-value statistic definition [F2]. The events $D_m$, $m\in M$, are pairwise disjoint and partition $\Omega$. Countable additivity [F3] gives $P_0(H\cap\{p_N\le u\})=\sum_{m\in M}P_0(H\cap D_m\cap\{p_N\le u\})$ and $P_0(H)=\sum_{m\in M}P_0(H\cap D_m)$. Summing the assumed stratum inequalities over the increasing enumeration of $M$ (equivalently, taking finite partial sums and then their limits) yields $P_0(H\cap\{p_N\le u\})\le uP_0(H)$. [given, F2, F3]

2.1 Let $Y_u$ be a version of $E_0[\mathbf1_{\{p_N\le u\}}\mid\mathcal F_1]$, which exists by [A1] and [F1]. The event identities in [F1] and [F4] turn step 1.1 into $\int_HY_u\,dP_0\le uP_0(H)$ for every $H\in\mathcal F_1$. Also $Y_u\ge0$ almost surely by [F5]. If $P_0(Y_u>u)>0$, then for some integer $k\ge1$ the set $H_k=\{Y_u\ge u+1/k\}\in\mathcal F_1$ has positive probability, because $\{Y_u>u\}=\bigcup_{k\ge1}H_k$. Monotonicity [F6] gives $\int_{H_k}Y_u\,dP_0\ge(u+1/k)P_0(H_k)>uP_0(H_k)$, contradicting the preceding event-integral bound. Thus $Y_u\le u$ almost surely. The argument is for each fixed $u$ and does not assert a common exceptional set over uncountably many thresholds. [A1, F1, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, choose, algebra] ∎

items.title: Conditional-error budget for two-stage adaptation
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P_0$ be one fixed null probability law on $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$,
and let $\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the interim sigma-algebra. Let
$R_0\in\mathcal F$ be the original design's rejection event, and let
$R_1\in\mathcal F$ be the adapted design's event of any eventual rejection,
including early and final decisions. Choose versions
$$A=E_0[\mathbf1_{R_0}\mid\mathcal F_1],\qquad Q=E_0[\mathbf1_{R_1}\mid\mathcal F_1].$$
For $\alpha\in[0,1]$, if $P_0(R_0)\le\alpha$ and $Q\le A$ almost surely,
then $P_0(R_1)\le\alpha$. The original conditional error $A$ is an
almost-sure class; changing its version does not change any rejection
probability.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** identify the mean conditional errors by the tower property, then compare their expectations.

1.1 By [A1] and [F1], both conditional-expectation classes exist. Since $0\le\mathbf1_{R_j}\le1$ for $j=0,1$, order preservation and the constant rule in [F2] give $0\le A,Q\le1$ almost surely. All representatives of either class agree almost surely by [F1], so the rejection probabilities do not depend on the chosen versions. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Let $\mathcal F_0=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}$. By [F3], $E_0[A\mid\mathcal F_0]=E_0[\mathbf1_{R_0}\mid\mathcal F_0]$. Each side is constant almost surely because it is $\mathcal F_0$-measurable; testing its defining event identity at $\Omega$ shows its constant is its ordinary expectation. Thus [F4] gives $E_0A=E_0\mathbf1_{R_0}=P_0(R_0)\le\alpha$. The same argument gives $E_0Q=P_0(R_1)$. Order preservation [F2], applied to $Q\le A$ with conditioning sigma-algebra $\mathcal F_0$, gives $E_0[Q\mid\mathcal F_0]\le E_0[A\mid\mathcal F_0]$; these constants are $E_0Q$ and $E_0A$, so $P_0(R_1)=E_0Q\le E_0A\le\alpha$. [F2, F3, F4, given] ∎

items.title: A conditionally superuniform stage-2 p-value preserves conditional error
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-conditional-error-budget-two-stage-adaptation]], let $p_2$ be a
measurable stage-2 p-value with values in $[0,1]$. Choose an
$\mathcal F_1$-measurable representative $A$ of the original conditional-error
class that takes values in $[0,1]$ everywhere; such a representative exists by
clipping any version on its null exceptional set. Changing to this version
changes $R_2$ only on a null set. Suppose that for every
fixed $u\in[0,1]$,
$$E_0[\mathbf1_{\{p_2\le u\}}\mid\mathcal F_1]\le u\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
Then the adapted rejection event $R_2=\{p_2\le A\}$ satisfies
$$E_0[\mathbf1_{R_2}\mid\mathcal F_1]\le A\quad\text{almost surely},$$
and hence $P_0(R_2)\le\alpha$. The conditional p-value inequality is assumed
separately for each fixed $u$; no common exceptional set over all
$u\in[0,1]$ is required.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** approximate the interim-measurable threshold from above by finite-valued thresholds, then pass to the decreasing limit.

1.1 Conditional order and the constant rule [F5] give $0\le A\le1$ almost surely. Clipping a version on the measurable null set where it leaves $[0,1]$ preserves its conditional-expectation class and changes $R_2$ only on a null set, so take $0\le A\le1$ everywhere. For each integer $n\ge1$, define $A_n=2^{-n}\lceil2^nA\rceil$. Its level sets are $\{A_n=0\}=\{A=0\}$ and $\{A_n=k2^{-n}\}=\{(k-1)2^{-n}<A\le k2^{-n}\}$ for $1\le k\le2^n$, so they are in $\mathcal F_1$. The inequality $\lceil2x\rceil\le2\lceil x\rceil$ shows $A_{n+1}\le A_n$, and $0\le A_n-A<2^{-n}$, hence $A_n$ is finite-valued and $A_n\downarrow A$. Write its values as $t_{n,k}=k2^{-n}$, $k=0,\ldots,2^n$, and put $S_{n,k}=\{A_n=t_{n,k}\}$. By [F2], the events $\{p_2\le t_{n,k}\}$ are measurable. Let $Q_n=E_0[\mathbf1_{\{p_2\le A_n\}}\mid\mathcal F_1]$. The disjoint partition by $S_{n,k}$, linearity [F5], and taking out the bounded known indicator [F3] give $Q_n=\sum_{k=0}^{2^n}\mathbf1_{S_{n,k}}E_0[\mathbf1_{\{p_2\le t_{n,k}\}}\mid\mathcal F_1]\le\sum_{k=0}^{2^n}t_{n,k}\mathbf1_{S_{n,k}}=A_n$ almost surely. For all $n$ these inequalities hold on one probability-one set, because only countably many fixed dyadic thresholds occur. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F5, given, choose, algebra]

2.1 The events $B_n=\{p_2\le A_n\}$ decrease to $B=\{p_2\le A\}$. Their complement indicators are bounded and hence integrable, and increase to $\mathbf1_{B^c}$. Thus [F4] gives $E_0[\mathbf1_{B_n^c}\mid\mathcal F_1]\uparrow E_0[\mathbf1_{B^c}\mid\mathcal F_1]$ almost surely. By linearity and the constant rule [F5], this is equivalent to $Q_n\downarrow Q:=E_0[\mathbf1_B\mid\mathcal F_1]$. Taking limits in step 1.1 and using $A_n\downarrow A$ yields $Q\le A$ almost surely. [F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F6] to $R_2=B$: its conditional rejection probability is the $Q$ of step 2.1 and is at most $A$, while the original conditional-error budget has expectation at most $\alpha$. Therefore $P_0(R_2)\le\alpha$. [F6, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Calibrated selected sample size and an uncalibrated weight change
items.statement:
In the finite null model below, the selected stage-2 sample size is a function
of interim information, and each selected-size p-value retains its conditional
null calibration. The rejection rule at the original conditional error has
null rejection probability $1/2$, equal to the original budget. In the normal
model, for any fixed critical value $c>0$, the equal-weight inverse-normal rule
rejecting when $(Z_1+Z_2)/\sqrt2\ge c$ has size
$\alpha=\int_c^\infty\phi(t)\,dt\in(0,1/2)$. Choosing unit-norm weights from
the sign of the interim statistic $Z_1$ and retaining $c$ raises that
probability to $3\alpha/2$.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The two null models and notation stated above; verify the calibrated finite-size rejection probability and the changed-weight normal rejection probability.

1.1 Put $\Omega=\{0,1\}^4$ with the uniform law and let $I,B_0,B_2,B_3$ be the independent fair-bit coordinates. Define $p_j=1/2$ when $B_j=0$ and $p_j=1$ when $B_j=1$, for $j\in\{0,2,3\}$. Each $p_j$ is measurable with values in $[0,1]$, and its null CDF is $0$ for $u<1/2$, $1/2$ for $1/2\le u<1$, and $1$ at $u=1$, so each is a valid p-value by [F3]. Let $\mathcal F_1=\sigma(I)$, select $N=2$ on $I=0$ and $N=3$ on $I=1$, and take the original rejection event $R_0=\{p_0\le1/2\}$. Independence and [A1, F4] give its conditional error $A=E_0[\mathbf1_{R_0}\mid\mathcal F_1]=1/2$ almost surely; [F5] makes the resulting event probabilities version-independent. For each $m\in\{2,3\}$ and $H\in\mathcal F_1$, independence of $B_m$ from $I$ gives $P_0(H\cap\{N=m\}\cap\{p_N\le u\})=c(u)P_0(H\cap\{N=m\})$, where $c(u)=0$ for $u<1/2$, $1/2$ for $1/2\le u<1$, and $1$ for $u=1$; in every case $c(u)\le u$. Thus [F1] makes $p_N$ conditionally superuniform. Rejection at $A=1/2$ is exactly the event that the selected bit is zero. Since $P_0(R_0)=P_0(B_0=0)=1/2$, set $\alpha=1/2$ in the overall conclusion of [F2] to obtain $P_0(p_N\le A)\le1/2$; the selected bit is fair, so equality holds and the original budget is attained. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 The positive density makes $\Phi$ continuous and strictly increasing. Define the one-sided stage p-values $p_i=1-\Phi(Z_i)$, so $Z_i=\Phi^{-1}(1-p_i)$; for $0<u<1$, $P_0(p_i\le u)=P_0(Z_i\ge\Phi^{-1}(1-u))=u$, and the endpoint inequalities are immediate, so they are valid by [F3]. Fix $c>0$ and set $\alpha=\int_c^\infty\phi(t)\,dt$, with $0<\alpha<1/2$ by positivity and evenness. Under the fixed equal-weight inverse-normal rule, reject when $W=(Z_1+Z_2)/\sqrt2\ge c$. The orthogonal change of variables $w=(z_1+z_2)/\sqrt2$, $v=(z_1-z_2)/\sqrt2$ has absolute Jacobian $1$ and satisfies $z_1^2+z_2^2=w^2+v^2$, so the joint density transforms to $\phi(w)\phi(v)$ and integration over $w\ge c$ gives the fixed-rule null rejection probability $\alpha$. [F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Choose $N_2=1$ when $Z_1\ge0$ and $N_2=2$ when $Z_1<0$. Without recalibrating $c$, use weights $w(N_2)=(1,0)$ in the first case and $(0,1)$ in the second; each has squared norm one. Since $c>0$, the adapted rejection event is the disjoint union $\{Z_1\ge c\}\cup\{Z_1<0,Z_2\ge c\}$, whose probability by independence is $\alpha+(1/2)\alpha=3\alpha/2>\alpha$. Thus unit-norm weights selected with the stage-2 size do not by themselves preserve the fixed-rule error probability. [given, step 1.2, construct, algebra] ∎
